note: Versioned CI gate baseline. Only the six reviewed high false positives are listed; each has an expected_count of 1 and a source review. The gate compares raw Rust Audit JSON by fingerprint and count, so a new high, a second occurrence of a reviewed pattern, or a stale entry fails. Keep the engine sha256 in step with .github/scripts/rust-audit-requirements.txt.

findings.message: Dependency `pprof` is not popular but is 2 edit(s) away from `approx` (potential typosquat).
findings.review: False positive R20: pprof 0.15 is a real crates.io package (cargo tree -i pprof proves it), optional behind the profile feature; approx is only a similarly spelled popular crate. pprof is intentional, documented in eqproxy-cli/Cargo.toml, and not a typosquat.

findings.message: build.rs executes an external command at compile time (supply-chain risk: code runs on every build).
findings.review: False positive R21: eqproxy-cli/build.rs runs the checked-in eqproxy-net/build-support/gen-test-certs.sh to create ephemeral test certificates in OUT_DIR. It uses no network and returns before Command::new for release builds; tests depend on the fixtures. The script is fixed source, not an invented dependency.

findings.message: Crate `rustc_ast` does not exist but is within 2 edit(s) of `rustc_hash` (near-miss / hallucinated name).
findings.review: False positive R18c: lints/eqproxy-lints is a rustc-private Dylint crate (#![feature(rustc_private)]); rustc_ast is supplied by the compiler sysroot, not crates.io. rustc_hash is a wrong near-miss suggestion for this context.

findings.message: `use rustc_errors::...` references a crate that is not declared in Cargo.toml (unresolved external identifier; compilation will fail).
findings.review: False positive R18a: rustc_errors is a compiler-private crate supplied by the rustc sysroot; lints/eqproxy-lints declares rustc_private and is built with the pinned nightly Dylint toolchain, not a crates.io dependency.
